### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **52** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/package.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**26** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 90106d62b259341f73b4c0757e99f4a1fdb148ac`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/package.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **179** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 90106d62b259341f73b4c0757e99f4a1fdb148ac` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `368226321d3939fe4cd488b29a01a2354701e128` — the merge of head `5901aa987bcda7f9d6beeadcb885cae73229f607` into base `90106d62b259341f73b4c0757e99f4a1fdb148ac`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 368226321d3939fe4cd488b29a01a2354701e128 && git checkout 368226321d3939fe4cd488b29a01a2354701e128
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 90106d62b259341f73b4c0757e99f4a1fdb148ac 5901aa987bcda7f9d6beeadcb885cae73229f607 && git checkout -B drift-repro 90106d62b259341f73b4c0757e99f4a1fdb148ac && git merge --no-ff 5901aa987bcda7f9d6beeadcb885cae73229f607

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 90106d62b259341f73b4c0757e99f4a1fdb148ac
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 90106d62b259341f73b4c0757e99f4a1fdb148ac` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9f64bd8a019ed09c1b5406abd7c0844fc6222a3b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/datasource-pull.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/datasource-window-read.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/pull-refusal.ts, packages/services/service-automation/package.json, packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/spec/liveness/mapping.json, packages/spec/liveness/job.json

Rendered by an isolated sub-agent of this seat at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Inputs: card #32062 (body and all ten comments), the slice-1 record 6774735605, the PR body, its 21 files, the net diff against `main` (merge base `fb37ef04`), and the check-runs on this head. Read-only: nothing was built, run or re-run. Code outside the diff was read at this head, never reviewed: ADR-0153 (D1, D2, D8, the children table), `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/external-organization-scope.ts` and `federated-phantom-anchors.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/tenant-field.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-data-crud.ts` (`findData`), `packages/types/src/query-read-limits.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/external-driver-floor.ts`, `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` (`collectSourcedMappingErrors`), `packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts`. The tests in the diff were read, not reviewed.

Check-runs on the head: 59 `success`, 9 `skipped` (opt-in harnesses, the queue verdicts, the live PG + MySQL temporal conformance job, UI published artifacts), none failed. `Test Core` 1/8 to 8/8, `Type Check · workspace`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset`, `Validate Package Dependencies` and `Dogfood Regression Gate` are `success`.

**Result: PASS, with two should-fix findings (④ S2, S3), each earning a delta review of its fix, and seven nits. S1 of the slice-1 record is closed on both edges.**

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The binder's accept set widens. Right.** `judgeJobPull` binds a mapping that declares `connectorSource` or `datasourceSource`; on `main` a `datasourceSource` mapping was refused at bind and its job not scheduled. No job that bound before is refused now. The no-source refusal keeps its key prefix and names both keys.
2. **`ConnectorSourcePullResult` changes from an interface to a union of two interfaces. Right for implementers, a compile-time tightening for readers.** An implementation answering the old shape still satisfies the connector arm (`source` optional). A TypeScript reader that reads `connector`, `action` or `watermark.target` without narrowing on `source` no longer compiles, and an interface can no longer extend the name. No such reader exists in this tree: `pullRunOutcomeOf` reads base fields and narrows before `object`. The changeset says so in words. Three new exports (`ConnectorSourcePullConnectorResult`, `ConnectorSourcePullDatasourceResult`, `ConnectorSourcePullResultBase`); `api-surface/contracts.json` and `export-origins/contracts.json` agree with the source.
3. **`ConnectorPullResult` in `@objectstack/service-automation` makes the same move. Right, same note.** It is a root export; the connector arm gains a required `source: 'connector'`, which is additive at run time.
4. **`ConnectorPullRefusalReason` gains four members. Right, additive.** `source_key_missing`, `source_binding_invalid`, `source_organization_scope_unstated`, `job_organization_missing`. The three ADR tokens are reused verbatim (carrier note 6762989212 item 3).
5. **`@objectstack/objectql` exports `resolveExternalRowCap`. Right, additive.** The function is unchanged.
6. **`refuseBlankMatchKeys` becomes an export of `connector-pull.ts` only; `index.ts` does not re-export it.** Not public surface.
7. **Run-time accept set of a connector pull: unchanged.** The dispatch to the datasource arm happens only when the artifact carries a `datasourceSource` object, and the strict schema lets no stored connector mapping carry one. The `no_connector_source` message changes its words; `code`, `status` and `reason` do not.
8. **Windowed reader: two commit rules and one reason change.** S1 lowers a commit in two cases and never raises one. N3 renames the reason of one over-cap case. On `main` the reader had no caller, so no caller sees a change.
9. **Liveness: five rows `planned` to `live`, three children gain their own `authorWarn`. Right.** The lint walker reads `authorWarn` at every depth of `children` (`packages/lint/src/lint-liveness-properties.ts`), so `full`, `deletePolicy` and `deletedField` still warn their author once the container's warning is dropped. `state-counts/mapping.md` (23 live, 10 planned of 33) matches.
10. **A new run-time dependency, `@objectstack/service-automation` on `@objectstack/plugin-security`. Sound; judged in ④ (a).**

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening) — the PR body's line, carried on the changeset. **Right for this diff.** It enlarges the public surface (① 2 to 5) and widens what the binder accepts (① 1). It narrows nothing that worked on `main`: every new refusal sits on a path that did not run before this slice (a `datasourceSource` pull was not scheduled), and a connector pull is refused exactly where it was. The card's own line is `no (narrowing)`; its real narrowings (D8's `job.organization` under `group` at boot and install, D3's incremental `mark` refusal) are not in this diff and stay owed by the slices that enforce them, each with its own line and ADR-0087 disposition.

`Metadata-protocol: semantic`. **Right.** No key, value or type is added or refused at parse. What changes is what an existing key means: `datasourceSource`, `object`, `watermark.field` and `watermark.start` go from parsed-and-warned to read. `semantic` outranks `added`, and nothing here is `narrowed`.

Level: `minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, the five packages whose published source the diff moves. That is the level the kind takes. `@objectstack/cli` changes one test and publishes nothing; `@objectstack/plugin-security` is not changed. Nothing is removed or renamed, so no migration table and no ADR-0087 marker is owed. The reader-side tightening of ① 2 is disclosed in the changeset body, which is the right place for it.

### ③ Boundary flags

The slice-2 report's two `open_questions` (6778135611) are answered by the seat in 6778809715, as seat-discretion calls:

1. **N2** (the row-cap refusal carries whole rows): B, an engine read option in its own later slice. Nothing in this diff widens N2: `judgeBounds` still reads the watermark field only. Still owed by the card.
2. **D8's read half in this slice**: A, it stays. I agree on the merits, see ④: the reader wired without it would copy every organization's rows.

Dev deviations:

- **(a) the plugin-security run-time dependency.** Accepted as sound; ④ (a), nit N1.
- **(c) four refusal reasons the ADR does not name.** Accepted; ④ (c).
- **Files outside the claim's list** (`packages/runtime`, the install-local remedy, three tests pinning the old words). Accepted: the seat's restated order (6774801890) names the binder, and the remedy is carrier note item 7. I read the new remedy against the tree: `os validate` does refuse a `pull` whose mapping declares neither source, so its last clause is true.
- **Liveness children gain `authorWarn`.** Right (① 9).
- **(d) `Skills-docs: none`.** Not true of the docs half; ④ nit N2. The seat rewrites the line before ACCEPT.
- **The stale JSDoc in `packages/spec/src/data/mapping.zod.ts`** ("READ BY NOTHING YET"). The carrier is named by the seat. It is a code comment; the generated reference row for `datasourceSource` reads true on this head.

Carrier note 6762989212, item by item: 1 is covered by the per-row value check; 2 is closed here (the pull judges the binding at run time); 3 is met; 7 is closed here. **Item 6 is still open**: a `synced` target that itself carries an `external` binding, a source object equal to the target, and an `upsertKey` no `fieldMapping` entry writes. The last one is not silent on this path (every row is refused for a blank match key and the run is `degraded`), but none of the three is named. The card stays open; a later slice or a dated ADR-0153 note owes them.

Not escalated: nothing here needs a maintainer ruling.

### ④ Design judgment

**The contract, `packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`, against D1 and its first consumer.** The union does what seat answer 1 (6773389044) ruled: a `source` discriminator, `connector` and `action` required on the connector arm, the datasource arm naming the object and the datasource. `source === 'datasource'` narrows both ways although the connector arm's `source` is optional, and the first consumer (`pullRunOutcomeOf`) does exactly that under a green type check. The datasource arm's fields match what `pullDatasourceSource` returns, field for field: `readPath` is the reader's own two values, `from` and `committed` are spelled in the field's storage form by `spellCanon`. Sentence by sentence against the code:

- "a connector pull rejects before anything is written; a datasource pull refused part-way through its read rejects too, keeping the windows it read to their end". True: every refusal throws, rows of earlier windows stay written.
- "a datasource source that is not a federated object" is refused. True (`source_binding_invalid`).
- "A pull whose rows the import runner refused RESOLVES". True on both arms.
- "the position this run committed at a window's end". **Ahead of the code, nit N3.**

**(b) S1 is closed on both edges, with a test each.** Read in `datasource-window-read.ts` at this head:

- *Absent high-water value.* `builtin()` now passes `pages > 1 ? (h1 ?? last.lo) : undefined`, so a multi-page open-above window whose high-water read found nothing commits at most its own `lo`. Test: "[S1] a multi-page window whose high-water read found nothing commits its own lo" (empty source at both high-water reads, five rows landing before page one, page size 2, `committed` equals `from`).
- *High-water value below `from`.* `commitWindow` takes `Math.max(capped, this.report.from)`. Test: "[S1] a commit never goes below where the run started" (source maximum at T+100, start at T+500, rows at T+600 and above landing after the read; `committed` equals `from` and every commit is at or above it).

Each test fails without its own half: the first would commit the largest value written, the second T+100. The floor at `from` is safe for the reason the comment gives. One residue, nit N7.

**The other invariants, on the wired path.** 10 holds: `organizationScope` builds the conjunct once and `scoped()` puts it on both high-water reads, every page and every floored window. 6 holds at run time (`source_key_missing` before any read). 1 holds (`watermarkKindOf`). 8 and 12 are unchanged from slice 1. The read path is chosen with the floor's own predicate, `needsExternalDriverFloor`, over the datasource definition, and a managed datasource is refused as D1 requires, which the build does not check (it reads only the `external` binding), so the run-time judgment is the stricter and the correct one.

**D8's read half against the ADR.** Under a walled posture: `walled` reads with `organization_id` equal to the job's organization; `shared` reads whole; `undeclared` and `tenant-field-unenforceable` are both refused as `source_organization_scope_unstated`, which is D8's "a source whose scope cannot be written as one of those". Under `single` nothing is added. The `null` answer of `externalOrganizationScopeOf` (not federated) is unreachable here, because the pull has already required an `external` binding and `isFederatedObject` reads the same key. The context key the pull reads, `tenantId`, is the one `jobExecutionContext` writes. If the served object definition ever fails the phantom-anchor identity test, the answer is `walled` and the predicate names a column the remote lacks, which fails toward no rows, never toward another organization's rows.

**(a) The plugin-security dependency.** Sound at run time. The two imports are a pure function and a string constant; they need no plugin registered, hold no state and involve no `instanceof`. No cycle: plugin-security's run-time dependencies are `core`, `formula`, `metadata-core`, `platform-objects`, `spec` and `types`, each already a run-time dependency of service-automation, so the published closure grows by plugin-security alone. A service depending on a plugin at run time has a precedent in the same manifest (`@objectstack/plugin-auth`). Reusing the one reading is the right call: `external-organization-scope.ts` says the boot refusal and the Layer 0 input must not re-derive the question, and a third copy in the pull would be exactly that. **The seam that should carry it is `@objectstack/core`'s security module, nit N1.**

**(c) The four reasons.** Each is honest and none should borrow an ADR token:

- `source_binding_invalid`: the ADR and the build name no token for "not a federated object", "on a managed datasource" or "a field no window can be halved on". The nearest ADR token, `watermark_not_exact`, means an integer that does not read back exactly; using it for a `text` field would mislabel the fault. One reason covers five conditions, told apart by the message.
- `job_organization_missing`: D8 says a pull job without an organization is "refused by name" at boot and install and gives no token. This is the run-time face of the same rule and the only thing between a walled source and a pull that cannot say whose rows to read. When the D8 slice lands its boot and install refusals, they should spell the same token.
- `watermark_start_invalid`: judged in the slice-1 record; unchanged.
- `mapping_target_refused`: already the connector pull's reason for a refused target field; widened here to "not registered" and "not `managedBy: 'synced'`". Same subject, the mapping's target.

One reuse is loose, nit N4.

**S2, should-fix: the run holds every row's result, and copies them all on every batch.** `sumSummaries` in `datasource-pull.ts` builds `results: [...a.results, ...b.results.map(...)]` after every page or window, and the sum is returned on the result. So a pull keeps one `ImportRowResult` per source row for the whole run, and each batch copies everything before it. At 1,000 rows a page the copying is quadratic in the row count: about 5,000 batches and on the order of 10^10 element copies for five million rows, and memory grows with the table. D1 makes a warehouse table "pullable at any size", and in this slice every scheduled run is a full read from `watermark.start`, so every run pays it. The contract does not want these rows: `ConnectorSourcePullSummary` is the counters, and its own doc says the per-row results are not the part a caller may read. Fix: sum the counters, and keep no per-row results across batches (or a bounded sample of the refused ones). Read, not run. No row is lost by it, which is why it is not a must-fix; a run that dies of it commits nothing.

**S3, should-fix: every read also runs a count.** The pull names a `limit` on every read, and `findData` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-data-crud.ts`) runs `engine.count` over the same `where` whenever a `limit` is present, unless the query says `count: false`. The pull does not say it, and reads only `records`.

- On the floored path the floor's `count` is `readCapped` again, so every window that answers under the cap is fetched from the remote twice. D2 says each window "is one plain `find` through the floor", and D1's "What they cost" counts the round trips; neither counts this one, and `report.reads` does not see it.
- On the built-in path each page adds a `count(*)` over the window's range and key cursor.

Fix: `count: false` on the pull's query (the door honours it and answers `hasMore` from the page alone). Read from the two files, not run: the diff's tests adapt the protocol straight onto `ql.find`, so they do not exercise the real door's count or its read limits. A case through the real `findData` would pin both S3 and the "every read names its own `limit`" claim.

Nits (none changes correctness or the contract):

- **N1. Where the scope reading lives.** Everything `externalOrganizationScopeOf` composes already sits below plugin-security (`isFederatedObject` in core, `isTenancyDisabled` in spec, `TENANT_SCOPE_FIELD_DEF` in metadata-core), and `core/src/security/tenant-layer0-verdict.ts` already takes its answer as an input. Moving the pure reading and `EXTERNAL_SCOPE_REMEDY` into core's security module, re-exported by plugin-security, would let the service depend on core alone and keep the plugin package out of every process that loads the automation service. Follow-up card; not this PR.
- **N2. `Skills-docs: none` is untrue of one hand-written page.** `content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx`, under "Pulling a mapping", says a source is "`connectorSource`, or `datasourceSource`, which the pull engine does not run yet". On this head the engine runs it. The same section's "Each run is one pull. It calls the connector's read action once, reads one response" is now true of a connector source only. The line's reason speaks to `skills/` alone (true: no skill names either key). Disposition: rewrite the PR-body line to `follow-up owed — content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx` for the seat to file, or correct the page here; it is a prose face. Method: `git grep` over the head's `content/docs` and `packages/spec/docs` for statements this diff makes false; the bot's own 26-row list was not printed and was not re-derived, since that is a local run. Pages that only name a changed package or symbol are not findings. `packages/spec/docs/SYNC_ARCHITECTURE.md` still says `defineStack` refuses a mapping "with no `connectorSource`"; that went stale with the spec child, not here, and the P3 guide child owns the file.
- **N3. The contract says "committed"; the code stores nothing yet.** `watermark.committed` is documented as "the position this run committed", and the result type's header speaks of "the position it committed". On this head `commit` is a no-op and the next run starts at `watermark.start` again; the module doc and the changeset say so, the published JSDoc does not. Carrier: the D7 slice, which makes the sentence true. Same class as slice 1's N4.
- **N4. `no_connector_source` for a malformed `datasourceSource`.** A `datasourceSource` with no `object` or no `watermark` is refused under that reason. The strict schema keeps a parsed mapping from reaching it, and the message is right; `source_binding_invalid` would name it better.
- **N5. "The keyed upsert makes the re-read harmless" overstates.** It is harmless to the rows. Until D7 every run rewrites every row from `watermark.start` with `runAutomations: true`, so record-triggered automations, audit rows and `updated_at` on the `synced` target move for every row on every run. The changeset should say that, and a release that ships this changeset before the D7 slice ships that cost. Carrier: the D7 slice, with the release order the seat already tracks for N1 of slice 1.
- **N6. Two stale sentences and one unjudged pair.** `scheduleAppArtifactJobs` still comments "(or has no `connectorSource`)" above the call it now makes for either source. `job.json`'s evidence still ends "one whose mapping declares no `connectorSource`" for `collectJobPullMappingErrors`. And the dispatch reads `datasourceSource` first, so an unparsed artifact carrying both sources is pulled as a datasource source without the exclusivity the parse enforces being named at run time.
- **N7. Hardening the floored read against a floor that is not there.** The read path is decided from the served datasource definition; the engine decided from the definition it registered. If the two ever differ and the driver is in fact unfloored, a floored window asks `limit` equal to the cap with no order and takes whatever comes back as the whole window. Asking for cap + 1 and refusing an answer over the cap would turn that into a loud refusal. Separately, S1's floor is `from`; `window.lo` is the tighter bound the comment's own argument supports, and with it a last-window commit could not fall below an earlier window's commit in the same run when the source's maximum drops between the two high-water reads. Both are conservative as written.

Slice-1 items: S1 closed (above). N3 closed: an unreadable non-NULL value over the cap is `watermark_not_exact`, a NULL still blames the driver, with a test. N4 closed: the `pull-refusal.ts` sentence is true now that `datasource-pull.ts` throws the type. N1 of slice 1 closed: the remedy can be followed. N2 remains owed (③ 1).

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-32062-sync-in-p2-engine`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYm8sWjp2Pk76warN7w`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review — delta

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5901aa987bcda7f9d6beeadcb885cae73229f607`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts (unchanged this round) + packages/services/service-automation/src/datasource-pull.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts, packages/spec/liveness/job.json

Delta on record 6779604367 (head `9f64bd8a`), rendered by an isolated sub-agent of this seat at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Inputs: the round's diff `9f64bd8a..5901aa98` (three commits, six files, +177 / −42), the dev's addendum 6780929437 on #32062, the PR body's three declaration lines, and the check-runs on this head. Read-only: nothing was built, run or re-run. Check-runs once the re-runs started by the PR-body edit had settled: 62 `success`, 11 `skipped`, none failed.
